text: Coverage: In the O365 activity data, the malicious link-file upload can appear as a FileUploaded event in sourcetype=o365:management:activity or sourcetype=ms:o365:management, and the complete FileUploaded listing shows exactly one uploaded .lnk file: BRUCE BIRTHDAY HAPPY HOUR PICS.lnk.
evidence: The complete FileUploaded population across both O365 activity feeds, grouped by extension, returned 5 of 5 rows and was read in full: five extensions (jpg, lnk, pdf, png, pptx), each present in both feeds (feeds=2). The lnk group contains exactly one file name, BRUCE BIRTHDAY HAPPY HOUR PICS.lnk, and no other extension group contains a .lnk. A detail cross-check listing all 14 FileUploaded rows (7 files x 2 feeds) confirmed the same: only one .lnk upload exists in the O365 activity data.

The complete 22-row lifecycle of this file shows the other 21 events are not uploads: FileAccessed/FileModified in the same seconds, the 09:58:02 AnonymousLinkCreated/SharingSet/SharingInheritanceBroken sharing events, and the 09:59:04+ AnonymousLinkUsed/FileAccessed events by bstoll@froth.ly, anonymous users, and app@sharepoint from other IPs with Edge/17.17134 or ExportWorker UAs. Only the FileUploaded record is the upload act, so its UserAgent is the answer.
rival: Any other FileUploaded event in the O365 activity data, including the six non-.lnk uploads and later link-use/share events on the same file.
